title: A Nuclear Test May Have Blasted a Manhole Cover Into Space

scenes.text: A manhole cover may have been shot into space by a nuclear bomb.
In 1957, scientists in Nevada sealed a steel cap over a shaft and set off a bomb below.
A high speed camera caught the cap in just one frame. Then it was gone.
One physicist estimated it left at 125,000 miles an hour. Five times escape speed.
Nobody ever found it. Many scientists think it simply vaporized.
So it either reached space, or turned to vapor. Nobody knows which.

description:
In 1957 a nuclear test in Nevada may have launched a steel manhole cover into space.
The Pascal-B test sealed a heavy steel cap over a shaft. A high speed camera caught it in a single frame, and physicist Robert Brownlee estimated about 125,000 mph. The cover was never found, and the number is a rough estimate, not a measurement. Many scientists think the cap vaporized.
Space or vapor? Tell us what you think.
first_comment: Brownlee himself said the speed number was only a rough estimate. Space or vapor: which do you pick?
